goal: `mc build ios` answers, without building, whether memoro needs a new iOS binary. The answer names the native paths and native dependencies that changed between the commit of the last shipped binary and the commit production runs. When nothing native changed it says `mc deploy` is all it takes, because the app loads its web code live from production (Capacitor `server.url`).

`mc build ios --device` builds memoro headless in its own background process and installs the app on the paired iPhone. `--testflight` builds, exports, verifies and, after a yes at the terminal, uploads to TestFlight. `--testflight --no-upload` stops at a verified IPA. No Xcode, Simulator or other GUI app is ever opened.

The binary always pairs with the web it will meet. It is built from the exact commit production runs, read from `/api/version`, or from a `--sha` that production already contains. Every binary carries that commit in Info.plist (`MemoroBuildCommit`). The built app is read back, and must state the declared bundle id, the declared production URL, every app-local plugin, the commit and the build number, before anything is installed or uploaded.

A TestFlight build number comes from App Store Connect (highest uploaded + 1), never from a file. Two binaries never share a number. Every build is a row in `~/mc/runner/log/ios-builds.tsv`, and the last uploaded row is what `mc build ios` compares against.
A build holds the heavy lane like a deploy does: the merger's heavy rounds and `mc gate` wait for it.
contract: Nothing here opens a GUI application. Never `npx cap open`, never `open`, never Xcode.app or Simulator.app, and no simulator is booted. `xcodebuild`, `xcrun devicectl`, `plutil`, `codesign` and memoro's own scripts only.

Nothing is uploaded without a yes at a terminal (`ask`, as `mc deploy` asks). Nothing is attached to an App Store version and nothing is submitted: the verb prints the `asc:attach-build` command and stops.
memoro is read only through its declaration `.mc/ios.json` (memoro project `docs/project/mc/ios-build-declaration`). No memoro path, bundle id or team id is written into memoro-cli's code.
`mc deploy` behaves exactly as today, except that its heavy-lane hold and a build's exclude each other.
out_of_scope: memoro's half: `.mc/ios.json`, `MEMORO_IOS_BUILD_NUMBER`/`MEMORO_IOS_BUILD_COMMIT` in `post-sync.sh`, the tracked ExportOptions.plist and `asc-list-builds.mjs --json` are memoro's `ios-build-declaration` project. This plan's checks by hand need it on memoro's main.
Attaching a build to a version, What's New, review submission and release: a person's act in App Store Connect (`asc:attach-build` is printed, never run).
Bumping the marketing version (`IOS_MARKETING_VERSION` in memoro's `post-sync.sh`): a commit in memoro, read back from the built app here.
A minimum-native-version gate in memoro's web or worker.
Signing in to Xcode or unlocking the keychain: when either is missing, the verb names the one thing a person does, and stops.

success_criteria.criterion: The question alone: `mc build ios` answers within 60 s, builds nothing and touches no worktree. It names the last shipped build (number and commit), the commit production runs, and the native paths and native packages that differ between them, or `no native change since build <n> — mc deploy is enough`.
success_criteria.check: From any directory: `time mc build ios; echo exit $?` prints those lines and exit 0 in under 60 s, and `git -C ~/.memoro/mc/build/memoro rev-parse HEAD` is unchanged (or the directory does not exist).

success_criteria.criterion: A device build lands on the phone, headless and paired. `mc build ios --device` builds the commit production runs and installs it on the paired iPhone, and the register row says `installed` with that sha. No GUI app starts.
success_criteria.check: With the iPhone paired and unlocked, in a terminal: `mc build ios --device` ends with `mc: installed memoro me <version> (<build>) from <sha> on <device>`. In a second terminal throughout: `while sleep 5; do pgrep -x Xcode; pgrep -x Simulator; done` prints nothing. Afterwards, `xcrun devicectl device info apps --device <id> --bundle-id app.meetmemoro.memoro` shows the app, `tail -1 ~/mc/runner/log/ios-builds.tsv` has outcome `installed`, and its sha equals `curl -s https://meetmemoro.app/api/version`'s `commit_full`.

success_criteria.criterion: A TestFlight build is verified before any upload. `mc build ios --testflight --no-upload` produces an IPA whose own Info.plist says the build number chosen from App Store Connect, the production commit and the declared bundle id, signed by Apple Distribution.
success_criteria.check: `mc build ios --testflight --no-upload` ends with `mc: built <ipa> — memoro me <version> (<n>) from <sha>; not uploaded`. Then `unzip -p <ipa> 'Payload/App.app/Info.plist' | plutil -extract CFBundleVersion raw -` prints `<n>`, and the same with `MemoroBuildCommit` prints the sha. `<n>` is one more than the highest `version` in memoro's `node scripts/asc-list-builds.mjs --json`.

success_criteria.criterion: The refusals that keep the pairing true. A `--sha` that production does not contain is refused before anything is built. So is a second build while one runs. A built app whose read-back disagrees with the declaration is never installed or uploaded.
success_criteria.check: `mc build ios --device --sha origin/main` refuses with `production runs <live>, which does not contain <sha> — mc deploy first` whenever origin/main is ahead of production. The read-back refusal is covered by the tests named in step 3.

documents.label: How mc deploy runs in its own process and holds the heavy lane

steps.title: The register, the declaration reader, and `mc build ios` the question
steps.done_when: `src/mc/ios-builds.js` (register) and `src/mc/ios-build.js` (declaration, native diff, the question) exist with their tests. `mc build ios` with no flag answers as in success criterion 1, `mc build ios --shipped <build> <sha>` records a seed row, the verb is registered, and the gate is green.
instruction: Why: memoro's iOS app is Capacitor with `server.url: https://meetmemoro.app`, so the binary runs whatever web code production serves. Only the native layer pairs with a commit: the five app-local Swift plugins, `post-sync.sh`, `capacitor.config.ts`, and the Capacitor packages built from `node_modules`. On 2026-10-18 a session had to work out by hand whether three merged steps needed a new binary. It also warned that new JS meeting an old plugin, or the reverse, gives mixed behaviour. This step answers that question from data. The build steps come after.

Register: new `src/mc/ios-builds.js`, shaped like `src/mc/deploys.js` (read it first and reuse its TSV helpers `tsvHeader`/`tsvRow`/`parseDeploys` by generalising them only if that is a small change; otherwise copy the 40 lines). File `join(workRoot(env), 'runner', 'log', 'ios-builds.tsv')`. Header: `started`, `ended`, `sha`, `kind` (`seed` | `device` | `testflight`), `version` (marketing), `build` (number), `live_commit` (what production ran at the start), `outcome` (`running` | `installed` | `built` | `uploaded` | `failed` | `refused`), `stopped_at`, `note`, `artifact` (IPA or .app path), `delivery`, `pid`. Exports: `iosBuildsPath`, `readIosBuilds`, `recordStart(row)`, `recordEnd(key, fields)` (key = `{ started, sha }` as in deploys.js), `runningIosBuild(env, { alive })` (the last `running` row whose pid lives), and `lastShipped(env)`: the last row with `kind` `testflight` and `outcome` `uploaded`, or `kind` `seed`, whichever is later. Writes go under `realLock` from `src/mc/register.js`, like deploys.js.

Declaration: new `src/mc/ios-build.js`. `memoroRepo(env)` finds the memoro checkout the way `mc deploy` does (`defaultRepos()` in `src/mc/brief-collect.js`, the entry named memoro). `readIosDeclaration(repoPath, { git })` reads `.mc/ios.json` from `origin/main` with `git show origin/main:.mc/ios.json`, never from the working tree, so a stale checkout cannot change the answer. It checks `schema_version` 1 and the keys memoro's plan declares: `project`, `scheme`, `bundle_id`, `team_id`, `server_url`, `setup`, `sync`, `export_options`, `env.build_number`, `env.build_commit`, `info_plist_commit_key`, `list_builds`, `upload`, `app_local_plugins`, `native_paths`, `native_dependency_prefixes`. It returns `{ ok, declaration }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`, where the reason names the missing key or says `memoro has no .mc/ios.json on origin/main yet (memoro project ios-build-declaration)`.

The native difference: `nativeChanges({ repoPath, from, to, declaration, git })`. (1) `git diff --name-only <from> <to>`, filtered to paths that start with one of `native_paths` (a path entry matches exactly, a directory entry ending in `/` by prefix). (2) Native packages: `git show <rev>:package-lock.json` at both ends, parsed. For every `packages['node_modules/<name>']` whose name starts with one of `native_dependency_prefixes`, compare `version`; report each added, removed or changed package as `<name> <old>→<new>`. `package-lock.json` changing for other packages is not a native change. Return `{ paths: [...], packages: [...] }`.

The question, `mc build ios` with no flag. First `git fetch origin` in memoro (failure is a warning and goes on with what is there). Read the declaration. Read production: `fetch(<server_url>/api/version)` with a 15 s timeout; `commit_full` is `live`. Unreachable means exit 1 with `production did not answer /api/version — cannot say what the app would meet`. Then `lastShipped`; when there is none, say `no shipped build is recorded — mc build ios --shipped <build> <sha> records the last one (memoro docs/releases/ios.md names it)` and treat every native path as changed. Otherwise print: `last shipped: build <n> from <short> (<date>)`, `production runs: <short>`, then either the changed paths and packages with `a new binary is needed — mc build ios --device to try it, --testflight to ship it`, or `no native change since build <n> — mc deploy is enough`. Also check `origin/main` against `live`: when origin/main has native changes that production lacks, add `origin/main has native changes production does not run yet (<paths>) — mc deploy first, then build`. Exit 0 in every answered case.

`--shipped <build> <sha>`: records a `seed` row (`ended` = `started`, `outcome` `uploaded`, `kind` `seed`) after checking that `<sha>` resolves in memoro (`git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`) and `<build>` is digits. This is how the register learns about builds made before the verb existed. Martin seeds it once with build 38 from `862a490` (memoro `docs/releases/ios.md` line 14); the step session must not write that row in the real register.

The verb: add `build: './mc/commands/build.js'` to `VERB_MODULES` in `src/mc-verbs.js`. `src/mc/commands/build.js` takes `ios` as its first positional and refuses anything else with the usage. Flags: `--device`, `--testflight`, `--no-upload`, `--sha <ref>`, `--device-id <id>`, `--shipped <build> <sha>`, `--follow`, `--json`. In this step only the question and `--shipped` work; `--device` and `--testflight` print `not yet: mc-build-ios step 2/3` and exit 2. Add the verb to `src/mc/help-text.js` beside `mc deploy`, with one line each for the question, `--device`, `--testflight [--no-upload]` and `--shipped`.

Tests, new `tests/mc/ios-build.test.js` and `tests/mc/ios-builds.test.js`, with a temporary git repository built in the test (commits that touch `cap-config/x.swift`, `public/js/a.js` and `package-lock.json` with a changed `@capacitor/core` and a changed `left-pad`) and an injected `fetch`. Cover: `nativeChanges` reports only the native path and only `@capacitor/core`; `readIosDeclaration` reads origin/main and not the working tree, and names a missing key; the question prints `no native change` when from equals to, names the paths otherwise, and adds the `mc deploy first` line when origin/main has a native change production lacks; an unreachable production is exit 1; no `lastShipped` gives the seed hint; `--shipped` refuses a sha that does not resolve and records a seed row that `lastShipped` then returns. Run with `MC_WORK_ROOT` in a temporary directory so the real register is never touched.
`mc gate tests/mc/ios-build.test.js tests/mc/ios-builds.test.js`, then `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. Add `changelog.d/build-ios-question.md` (`section: Added`).

steps.title: mc build ios --device: the builder in its own process, the heavy lane, the read-back, the install
steps.done_when: `mc build ios --device` runs its preflights in the asking process, then starts the builder detached with its log at `~/mc/runner/log/ios-build.log`, and the terminal follows it (^C stops watching only). The builder holds the heavy lane as `mode: 'ios-build'`, builds the commit production runs in `~/.memoro/mc/build/memoro` with a real `npm ci`, reads the built app back against the declaration, and installs it with `devicectl`. `mc gate` waits for a build as it waits for a deploy. The tests below are green, and success criterion 2 is checked by hand if the phone is paired.
instruction: Read first: `src/mc/commands/deploy.js` (`run`, `startDeployerDefault`, `followDeploy`, `holdHeavyLane`, `waitForGate`, `ship`), `src/mc/deploy-run.js`, `src/mc/await-deploy.js` and `src/mc/gate-lock.js`. The builder is the deployer's shape: a detached process with the job as JSON, its output in one log, a row written before it starts and completed when it ends. `holdHeavyLane` is on main since #974 (2026-10-18).

Heavy lane for builds too: in `src/mc/await-deploy.js`, export `HEAVY_HOLD_MODES = ['deploy', 'ios-build']` and make `deployHolding` true for either mode (keep its name and exports; update its comment and the waiting line to `waiting for the <deploy|iOS build> (pid …)`, chosen from the lock's mode). `holdHeavyLane(job, deps)` in `commands/deploy.js` takes `mode` from `deps.mode ?? DEPLOY_MODE`; the builder passes `'ios-build'`. Extend `tests/mc/await-deploy.test.js` with an `ios-build` hold that is waited for.

Preflights, in the asking process, before anything is started. Each one fails fast with one line that names the fix. (1) Another build: `runningIosBuild` gives `an iOS build is running (pid …) — mc build ios --follow`, exit 2. (2) Xcode: `xcrun xcodebuild -version` with a 30 s timeout, else `Xcode command-line build tools are not usable here: <first line>`. Never `xcode-select --install`. (3) Signing identity: `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` must list an `Apple Development:` identity, else `no Apple Development signing identity in the login keychain — sign in to Xcode once (Settings → Accounts) on this Mac`. (4) The phone: `xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output <tmp file>` with a 60 s timeout. Choose the devices whose `hardwareProperties.platform` is iOS and whose `connectionProperties.pairingState` is `paired`, then `--device-id` among them when given, else exactly one. None gives `no paired iPhone — connect and unlock it, trust this Mac`; several gives a list with `--device-id <id>`. Read the field names from the real JSON on this machine and pin them in a fixture. (5) The commit: `git fetch origin` in memoro, then `live` from `<server_url>/api/version` (`commit_full`). Without `--sha` the target is `live`. With `--sha <ref>`, resolve it in memoro; it must be an ancestor of or equal to `live` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <live>`), else `production runs <short live>, which does not contain <short sha> — mc deploy first`, exit 1. The target must also be on origin/main (`--is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`), else refuse. (6) The declaration from origin/main (step 1).

Then the start: write the `running` row (`kind` `device`, `sha`, `live_commit`, `pid` of the builder), start `src/mc/ios-build-run.js` detached exactly as `startDeployerDefault` starts the deployer (installed script, own process group, stdin ignored, output truncated into `~/mc/runner/log/ios-build.log`). Print `mc: building memoro <short sha> for <device name> in its own process (pid …) — ^C stops watching, not the build; mc build ios --follow watches again`, then follow the log like `followDeploy`. `--follow` alone follows a running build or says `no iOS build is running`.

The builder (`buildIos(job, deps)` in `src/mc/ios-build.js`, called by `ios-build-run.js`). Each external command goes through one `step(label, argv, { cwd, env, timeoutMs })` helper. The helper prints `▸ <label>` and streams output to the log. On timeout it sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 s, and fails with `stopped_at` = label. Keep the last 64 KB of output for the failure note. Order:

(a) `holdHeavyLane(job, { mode: 'ios-build' })`, released in `finally`. (b) Worktree `join(mcHome(env), 'build', 'memoro')`. When absent, `git -C <memoro> worktree add --detach <dir> <sha>`. Otherwise `git -C <dir> checkout --detach --force <sha>` then `git -C <dir> clean -ffdx`, which removes `ios/` and `node_modules` so nothing generated survives from a previous build. Then assert `rev-parse HEAD` equals sha and `status --porcelain` is empty, else fail `worktree`. (c) `npm ci` (30 min). It must be a real install, never memoro's `deps:prepare` shared-cache link: `scripts/patch-contacts-spm.sh` edits a package in `node_modules` in place. (d) Each `setup` command of the declaration (`npx cap add ios`, 10 min). (e) The `sync` command (`npm run cap:build`, 20 min) with env `<env.build_commit>=<sha>`. For a device build, set no build number, so the declaration's default stands. (f) `xcodebuild -project <project> -scheme <scheme> -configuration Release -destination generic/platform=iOS -derivedDataPath <mcHome>/build/ios-derived -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath <mcHome>/build/ios-spm -allowProvisioningUpdates build` (60 min). The two fixed directories keep SPM checkouts and module caches warm between builds, because a new path each time would be a cold build. On failure, recognise `errSecInternalComponent` or `User interaction is not allowed` (keychain locked: `security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` in your own terminal) and `No Account` / `requires a development team` (sign in to Xcode once). Put the one-line fix in the note.

(g) The read-back, a pure `readBack({ appDir, declaration, sha, build })` given file reads and a `plutil` runner. Read the built `App.app` (`<derived>/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/App.app`). Its `Info.plist` (`plutil -convert json -o - <plist>`) must have `CFBundleIdentifier` = `bundle_id` and `<info_plist_commit_key>` = sha, and `CFBundleVersion` = the build number when one was set. Record `CFBundleShortVersionString` as `version`. Its `capacitor.config.json` must have `server.url` = `server_url`, and `packageClassList` must contain every `app_local_plugins` entry. Then `codesign --verify --deep --strict <App.app>`. Any difference fails with `stopped_at` `read-back` and names each one (`MemoroBuildCommit is 1a2b…, expected 3c4d…`). Nothing is installed.

(h) Install: `xcrun devicectl device install app --device <id> <App.app>` (10 min). Then complete the row (`outcome` `installed`, `version`, `build`, `artifact`) and print `mc: installed memoro me <version> (<build>) from <short sha> on <device name>`. Every failure completes the row as `failed` with `stopped_at` and the note. A throw does the same and goes on up, as `ship` does.
Tests, `tests/mc/ios-build-device.test.js`, with every external command injected (a fake `step` recording argv, cwd and env) and no real git, Xcode or device:
- The preflights: each refusal message, including no paired device, two devices without `--device-id`, and a `--sha` that production lacks.

- The builder's command order and arguments. `npm ci` comes before setup, setup before sync. The sync env carries the commit and no build number. xcodebuild has the two fixed paths and `-allowProvisioningUpdates`.
- `readBack` passes a matching app. It fails, naming each field, on a wrong commit, a wrong bundle id, a `server.url` of `http://localhost:8787`, and a missing `MemoroCameraPlugin`.
- A failed read-back never calls install.
- The row goes running → installed, and running → failed with `stopped_at`.
- The heavy lane is taken as `ios-build` and released on failure.
Then `mc gate` those files plus `tests/mc/await-deploy.test.js tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js tests/mc/gate-command.test.js`.

Check by hand, only when memoro's `.mc/ios.json` is on memoro's main and the iPhone is paired (`xcrun devicectl list devices`): run success criterion 2 and paste the last 20 log lines and the `pgrep` watch result into the PR body. If either is missing, say which in the PR body and leave the check to Martin. The tests are this step's gate.
`mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. Add `changelog.d/build-ios-device.md` (`section: Added`).

steps.title: mc build ios --testflight: the number from App Store Connect, archive, export, the IPA read back, the question, the upload
steps.done_when: `--testflight` chooses the build number from App Store Connect, archives and exports with the declaration's ExportOptions.plist, reads the number, commit and Distribution signature back out of the IPA itself, asks before uploading, uploads with memoro's upload script, records the row, and prints the `asc:attach-build` command without running it. `--no-upload` stops at the verified IPA. Old archives are pruned to the last five. The tests below are green, success criteria 3 and 4 are checked as far as this machine allows, and every `success_criteria[].met` that was checked is true.
instruction: Why: the documented manual procedure (memoro `docs/releases/README.md` § Submitting an iOS build) had three traps. The build number was a committed constant, so two different trees could carry one number. The local ExportOptions.plist let Xcode rewrite `CFBundleVersion` at export (`manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber`). And nothing checked that the IPA said what was meant. memoro's `ios-build-declaration` project gives this step a tracked ExportOptions.plist with that switch off, the `MEMORO_IOS_BUILD_NUMBER` override, and `asc-list-builds.mjs --json`.

The number, in the asking process after the step-2 preflights. Instead of the `Apple Development` check, require an `Apple Distribution:` identity. Run the declaration's `list_builds` argv with cwd the memoro checkout (its script reads App Store Connect credentials itself; mc never reads `.dev.vars` or any key). Parse `builds[].version` as integers and set `next = max + 1`. If the call fails, exit 1 with `App Store Connect did not answer (<first stderr line>) — no build number can be chosen`. Never fall back to a file.

The question, before the builder starts and only at a terminal (`interactive`/`ask` from `src/mc/prompt.js`, as `mc deploy` asks). With `--no-upload` the question is skipped, because nothing leaves the machine. The question reads: `upload memoro me (build <next>) from <short sha> — production runs <short live> — to TestFlight after it is built and verified? [y/N]`. Anything but yes records a `refused` row and exits 1. The yes goes into the job (`upload: true`). A non-interactive run without `--no-upload` is refused with `mc build ios --testflight asks before it uploads — run it in a terminal, or add --no-upload`.

The builder, after step 2's (a)–(e). The sync env also carries `<env.build_number>=<next>`. Instead of `build`: (f) `xcodebuild … -configuration Release -destination generic/platform=iOS -derivedDataPath … -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath … -archivePath <mcHome>/build/archives/<next>/App.xcarchive -allowProvisioningUpdates archive`. (g) `readBack` on `<archive>/Products/Applications/App.app` with `build: next`. (h) `xcodebuild -exportArchive -archivePath <archive> -exportOptionsPlist <worktree>/<export_options> -exportPath <mcHome>/build/archives/<next>/export -allowProvisioningUpdates`. (i) The IPA is the one `.ipa` in the export directory. Unzip `Payload/App.app` into a temporary directory and run `readBack` on it again: this catches an export that changed the number. Then check that `codesign -dvv <tmp>/Payload/App.app` (stderr) has an `Authority=Apple Distribution:` line. On failure, stop at `export-read-back`; nothing is uploaded.
(j) Without `upload` (`--no-upload`): complete the row `built` with `artifact` = the IPA, and print `mc: built <ipa> — memoro me <version> (<next>) from <short sha>; not uploaded`.

(k) With `upload`, first ask App Store Connect again (`list_builds`): if `<next>` exists by now, fail `number-taken`, because the binary is stamped and is not renumbered. Then run the declaration's `upload` argv with the IPA path appended, cwd the build worktree, timeout 30 min. Read a delivery id from its output if it prints one (`Delivery UUID: <uuid>` or similar; capture it with a regex and leave it empty if absent). Complete the row `uploaded` with `delivery`. Print `mc: uploaded memoro me <version> (<next>) from <short sha>` and then `next, by hand when it has processed: npm run asc:attach-build -- <version> <next> --wait (in memoro)`.
Prune: after a successful build or upload, keep the five newest directories under `<mcHome>/build/archives/` and remove the rest. Never remove the one just made.
Tests, `tests/mc/ios-build-testflight.test.js`, with everything injected:
- `next` is max + 1 over unordered versions; a failing `list_builds` is exit 1 with the message.
- The question: no gives a refused row; non-interactive without `--no-upload` is refused; `--no-upload` asks nothing.
- The command order: archive, read-back, export, IPA read-back, upload. A wrong `CFBundleVersion` in the IPA stops at `export-read-back` and never uploads.
- A missing `Authority=Apple Distribution` stops the same way.
- A number taken between the question and the upload gives `number-taken` and no upload.
- The delivery id is captured when printed.
- Pruning keeps five and never the current one.
- The attach command is printed and never run.

Check by hand, when memoro's declaration project is on main: run success criterion 3 (`--no-upload`, so nothing leaves the machine) and success criterion 4's `--sha origin/main` refusal when origin/main is ahead of production. Paste both into the PR body. Do not run an upload: the first real upload is Martin's, at his terminal.
Docs, in a last commit that touches nothing else:

- New `docs/technical/mc-build-ios.md`. Cover: why the binary is built from the commit production runs (Capacitor `server.url`); the question; the preflights; the builder's order with the fixed derived-data and SPM paths; the read-back and what it compares; how the number is chosen; the register; the heavy lane; what it never does (GUI apps, attaching, submitting).
- A row in `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`.
- `changelog.d/build-ios-testflight.md` (`section: Added`).
Then set every checked `success_criteria[].met` to true in the same PR.
`mc gate tests/mc/ios-build-testflight.test.js tests/mc/ios-build-device.test.js tests/mc/ios-build.test.js`, then `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.
